Senses.Explanation: Unable to account for it or sort it out. The phrase occurs 100 times in 63 allowlisted texts and appears both as self-report and as an interview verdict. An unnamed questioner says he cannot account for a distinction between expounding teachings and responding to the occasion; Yuan’an Feng tells another questioner, ‘Look at you, unable to account for it’; and Yuan’an, Linye Tongqi, and Linye Tongqi’s later lamp-record version use it of their own inability to settle a fan-name test, a north-or-south salutation, or which recorded saying is deep or shallow. Zhaozhou Congshen’s ‘the highest way is not difficult’ exchange supplies a famous duration formula: he says someone once asked him and he was unable to account for it for five years. Yuan’an’s later letter turns the verb back on the reader: if unable to account for it, one must carefully account for it.
Senses.Note: The Zen deviation lies in public interview: ordinary inability to explain becomes both the participant's admission and the examiner's verdict, while masters also use it of their own inability. 'Explain,' 'distinguish,' and 'sort out' are contextual English renderings of the same act of furnishing an account, not different things; the corpus does not warrant multiple senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：至道無難，唯嫌揀擇。是時人窠臼否？師曰：曾有人問我，老僧直得五年分疏不下。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄), Zhaozhou Congshen section. Zhaozhou Congshen is the exact speaker who says that after someone asked him, he remained unable to account for it for five years.

Occurrences.Kwic: 云：王爺還是演教？還是酬機？王云：先演教，後酬機。云：衲子分疏不下。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄), Recorded Sayings of Prince Yong. The exact headword-bearing speaker is an unnamed questioning monk: after asking whether the prince expounds teachings or responds to the occasion, he says that this patch-robed monk cannot explain it. All six rungs leave him unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「和尚不妨著眼。」師云：「老僧分疏不下。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linye Qi (林野奇禪師語錄), exchange with Pomeng. Linye Tongqi is the exact speaker: after Pomeng tells him to apply his eye, Linye says that this old monk cannot account for it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 山僧到者裏直是分疏不下，正不知那一句是深、那一句是淺？那一則是難、那一則是易？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuan’an Feng (遠菴僼禪師語錄). Yuan'an Feng is the exact speaker who says that at this point he simply cannot account for which saying is deep, shallow, difficult, or easy.

Occurrences.Kwic: 居士向者裏還分疏得下麼？分疏看。若分疏不下，直須仔細分疏
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuan’an Feng (遠菴僼禪師語錄), Yuan'an Feng’s reply to layman Wu Shiban. Yuan'an asks whether the addressee can account for it and tells him to do so carefully if he cannot.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師與念尼王海憲相見次，公曰：還是南禮北禮？師曰：山僧分疏不下。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Linye Tongqi section. Linye Tongqi is the exact respondent who says that this mountain monk cannot account for whether the greeting should be southern or northern.
